courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Topics in Intensive Indigenous Language of Latin America I
courses.description: Introduction to an indigenous language of Latin America. Designed to provide students with the basics of grammar and vocabulary; the to ability to engage in simple, colloquial conversation; and basic writing skills as foundation for further study. The equivalent of six lecture hours a week for one semester. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: First-Year Ancient Mayan I
courses.description: Introduction to the grammar and hieroglyphic writing used to record Ancient Mayan as well as key elements of cultural and historical context that are crucial for interpreting texts, including calendrics and political history. Four lecture hours a week for one semester.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: First-Year K'iche' Maya I
courses.description: Introduction to K'iche' sounds, pronunciation, and language. Four lecture hours a week for one semester.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: First-Year Ancient Mayan II
courses.description: Explore basic functions of the script and language, how hieroglyphic texts are structured, and how the rich Classic Maya iconographic tradition interacts with and complements the textual tradition. Four lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 406.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: First-Year K'iche' Maya II
courses.description: Practice and further explore K'iche' sounds, pronunciation, and language. Four lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 406K.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Topics in Intensive Indigenous Language of Latin America II
courses.description: Continuation in the study of an indigenous language of Latin America. Designed to introduce students to advanced subjects in grammar and vocabulary and develop advanced conversation, reading, and writing skills as a foundation for further study. The equivalent of six lecture hours a week for one semester. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 601C with a grade of at least C.
courses.prereqText: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 601C with a grade of at least C.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Second-Year Ancient Mayan I
courses.description: Analyze problems in grammar and discourse in Ancient Mayan texts. Translate and interpret texts in detail to understand their structure, context, and broader meaning and purpose in their specific cultural and historical contexts. Examine the methods and tools of Maya epigraphy. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 407.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Second-Year Ancient Mayan II
courses.description: Analyze calendrics, rhetorical structure, and variation in script and language from the earliest to the latest hieroglyphic inscriptions. Explore the latest advances and current debates in the research and humanistic study of Ancient Mayan language and hieroglyphic writing. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 312K.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Second-Year K'iche' Maya I
courses.description: Explore complex everyday interactions: questions about people and events, states, and changes of state. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 407K.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Second-Year K'iche' Maya II
courses.description: Introduction to syntactic parallelism, as a stylistic and poetic resource, and K'iche' dialectology. Explore normal and inherent possession constructions and their cultural meaning in K'iche' society. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 312M.

courses.subject: LAL
courses.title: Topics in Third-Year Indigenous Language of Latin America I
courses.description: Advanced study of an indigenous language of Latin America, with an emphasis on advanced conversation and reading skills. Particular attention is given to cultural issues and discussion in the target language. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 611C with a grade of at least C.

courses.description: Intensive cultural and literacy-focused training in an indigenous language at the beginning level in preparation for research. Six lecture hours a week for one semester. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of graduate adviser.

May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Indigenous Languages of Latin America 385K and consent of graduate adviser.
